title: Inflation rises to 3.1%, as fuel prices push higher: StatsCan
summary: Statistics Canada says the pace of inflation picked up in September, as prices for gasoline climbed at a faster rate than in August.

image.caption: A truck passes an Esso station in Toronto on April 20, 2026, where gasoline was listed at 161.9 cents per litre. (Oksana Shtohryn/CBC)

blocks.text: Statistics Canada says the pace of inflation picked up in September, as prices for gasoline climbed at a faster rate than in August.
Gas prices rose at a quicker pace in September than in August, according to Statistics Canada
The national inflation rate rose to 3.1 per cent in September, according to data released by Statistics Canada on Monday.
The agency says the annualized inflation reading for September was boosted by higher prices for gasoline last month. Food prices also rose, but at a slower pace than in September.
Ahead of Monday’s release, a Bloomberg survey of 12 economists predicted the September consumer price index would rise 3.18 per cent year over year.

Jeff Lagerquist is a senior writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Erin, Ont., he studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. Jeff previously worked as a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance Canada. He was also a reporter and digital producer for CTV National News, BNN Bloomberg and The Financial Post. In 2025, he was a Columbia University energy journalism fellow.
